overview: Greece is a country in south-eastern Europe, at the southern end of the Balkan peninsula. Its capital, Athens, was a centre of ancient Greek civilisation, which gave the world early ideas of democracy, philosophy and theatre, as well as the Olympic Games. Modern Greece won its independence from the Ottoman Empire in the 1820s, and it joined what is now the European Union in 1981.

geography.text: Greece is a mountainous country with a very long coastline and thousands of islands spread across the Aegean and Ionian seas. Crete is the largest island. Mount Olympus, home of the gods in Greek myths, is the highest mountain. Summers are hot and dry, and winters are mild along the coasts.

history.text: Ancient Greek city-states such as Athens and Sparta developed ideas about democracy, philosophy, science and theatre that still shape the world. Greece later became part of the Roman, Byzantine and Ottoman empires. It won independence in the 1820s, was occupied in the Second World War, and after military rule from 1967 to 1974 became a democracy again.

events.title: First recorded Olympics
events.text: The first Olympic Games on record are held at Olympia.

events.title: Democracy in Athens
events.text: Athens introduces a system of government by its citizens.

events.title: Fall of Constantinople
events.text: The Byzantine capital falls to the Ottomans.

events.title: War of Independence
events.text: Greeks rise against Ottoman rule; independence follows within a decade.

events.title: Democracy restored
events.text: Military rule ends and Greece becomes a republic.

government.text: Greece is a parliamentary republic. Its 300-member parliament, the Hellenic Parliament, chooses the Prime Minister, who leads the government. The President, elected by parliament, is head of state. Greece joined what is now the European Union in 1981 and uses the euro.

economy.text: Tourism and shipping are the pillars of the Greek economy. Greek owners control one of the largest merchant fleets in the world, and tens of millions of tourists visit each year. Greece also produces olive oil, feta and fruit. A deep debt crisis from 2009 led to years of hardship.

culture.text: Ancient Greece gave the world democracy, the Olympic Games, theatre and philosophers such as Socrates, Plato and Aristotle. Many English words come from Greek. The Mediterranean diet, with olive oil, vegetables and fish, is listed by UNESCO as heritage shared with other countries.

items.title: The Acropolis
items.text: The rocky hill in Athens topped by the Parthenon, built in the 400s BC.

items.title: Greek myths
items.text: Stories of Zeus, Athena and Hercules still inspire books and films.

items.title: Delphi
items.text: Ancient Greeks believed it was the centre of the world.

sport.text: Greece is the birthplace of the Olympics. The first modern Olympics were held in Athens in 1896, and the city hosted again in 2004. In football, Greece shocked Europe by winning Euro 2004, and basketball is hugely popular.

items.title: Euro 2004
items.text: Greece won the European Championship as outsiders, beating hosts Portugal in the final.

items.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo
items.text: NBA champion and two-time Most Valuable Player.
